claims.claim: Direct human absolute oral bioavailability measurements for closely related sulfated/polar molecules are all well below 20%: pentosan polysulfate <1% to ≤3% (C06, C11, C19, C29), dextran sulfate poor (C09), zanamivir ~2% (C01, C03, C12), glucoraphanin ~5% (C14), acamprosate ~11% (C02, C04, C16), and N-acetylcysteine SR ~6-7% (C13).

L5 Caco-2 permeability records for polar glycosides and aminoglycosides show low absorptive permeability: paromomycin negligible in both directions (C58), breviscapine 4.78×10^-7 cm/s below the 1×10^-6 cm/s threshold (C66), baicalin 0.01-0.02×10^-6 cm/s at 4°C (C56), quercetin 3-O-glucuronide 0.11×10^-6 cm/s (C61), acteoside 0.24-0.34×10^-6 cm/s (C57, C62), echinacoside 0.76×10^-6 cm/s (C55), morroniside 0.55-0.62×10^-6 cm/s (C60), and PGA5 lower than mannitol (C59).

The single higher in vitro value, tobramycin sulphate control Papp 1.78×10^-6 cm/s (C64), is not an oral bioavailability measurement and does not establish F≥20% for the query; no L5 record provides direct F or query-specific efflux/metabolism data.

The query's extreme polarity, full ionization, and very low estimated logD are consistent with the low-permeability profile of these analogs; no affirmative threshold-relevant evidence supports F≥20%.
